newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open higher on Thursday, with technology shares boosted by the $6.6 billion merger of 3Com Corp and U.S. Robotics Corp.
Analysts said markets were likely to shrug off Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's warning that share prices may be overvalued.
The Dow Industrials fell more than 100 points following his remarks on Wednesday, but later staged a partial recovery. The index closed down 55 points at 6,983.
"It's really rather remarkable how Wall Street has taken the Greenspan thing relatively in (its) stride," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfallia Research, said markets were likely to focus on economic data due later in the day , looking for indicators on inflation and a possible Fed tightening of interest rates.
